_comment_emission_scale: CREATURE-PRESENTATION 2026-08-23. TUNABLE. The creature glbs ship self-lit -- the painted albedo is also the emission map, at full energy -- so in daylight every creature renders as its own texture plus an unshaded copy of itself. Measured on mudsnout: albedo hue 24 / sat 0.63 / value 0.37, rendered body a pale peach with the value contrast around the eyes gone. Halving it keeps the emission that makes a creature readable at dusk and in the Warrens while giving the colourways back their saturation and their faces. Consumed by creature_visual.gd::emission_scale(), applied in creature_body.gd::_swapped_material().
_comment_contact_shadow: CREATURE-LEGIBILITY-0903 (Gate 2.4, docs/ROADMAP.md). The 'ground-contact shadow' lever: the Compatibility renderer this project ships has no SSAO (tools/survey.sh), so nothing pins a creature's feet to the ground the way a real shadow would, and a small body in tall grass reads as standing IN the field rather than on it. A flat, unshaded, soft-edged ellipse under `creature_body.gd`'s own model origin (shaders/creature_contact_shadow.gdshader), applied to every creature body with a loaded model -- this is a grounding cue every creature is missing, not a per-species legibility tune, so unlike `field_rim`/`field_emission`/`field_degreen` it has no per-species opt-in. `radius_scale` multiplies the creature's own gameplay `radius` (never its art scale, same discipline `apply_size_multiplier`'s own header argues for -- the shadow is a fact about the collider's footprint, not a look). `opacity` is the blob's peak alpha at its centre before `core_fraction`'s falloff. TUNABLE.
_comment_field_bright_ceiling: OP-0905-03 (docs/owner/OWNER_PLAYTEST_2026-09-05.md, 'Bramblebun colour is awful'). `field_emission`/`field_degreen` (data/creatures/species.json) used to feed a raw, uncapped multiply -- at Bramblebun's shipped field_emission 2.5 that is a 3.5x push on R/B, and direct inspection (tools/_probe_field_bright_values.gd) shows these materials' un-brightened tint is already a flat white (1,1,1) over a textured base, so 3.5x pushes the coat's own mean pixel value (measured 0.49/0.37/0.21) to a mean of ~1.73 on the brightest channel -- deep in ACES's clip range, reading exactly as the owner called it: flat, washed-out, texture crushed. This is the soft-knee's target ceiling (creature_body.gd::_soft_knee_bright()): identity below the neutral 1.0 baseline (so a species with field_emission 0 is untouched), smoothly bending toward this value above it, never reaching it. 1.75 keeps Bramblebun's own brightest channel (R) at a rendered mean of ~0.85 -- comfortably under 1.0, so the coat keeps real light/shadow variation instead of clipping flat -- while still lifting every species that uses this lever meaningfully above their un-pushed baseline (Bramblebun 1.72x, Mudsnout 1.71x, Terrapup 1.63x at their shipped field_emission, per that probe's own printed numbers). A ceiling below 1.0 (floated as this key's first default) was rejected: since the baseline tint here IS 1.0, not a <1 base colour, any ceiling under 1.0 would darken every brightened species below its own normal shipped look -- reintroducing the exact 'creature disappears in the grass' problem this lever exists to fix. TUNABLE -- re-measure against tools/_probe_grass_separation.gd's render-based sweep (this pass only verified it numerically, not against a real render) before treating 1.75 as settled.
